name: wrong-join
description: Finance says the revenue report is off: an account with no orders this period dropped off it entirely, and some big accounts' totals look inflated compared to the ledger. Fix the report so every customer appears with their correct revenue.
bugs: the report query INNER JOINs customers to orders, so customers with no orders this period are dropped from the report instead of showing 0 revenue

the query also joins orders to the one-to-many line_items table and then SUM(o.amount) over that fanned-out result, so an order's amount is counted once per line item — revenue is inflated for any order with more than one line item

regression_check.cmd: python3 -c "import sqlite3,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from report import get_revenue_report; conn=sqlite3.connect(':memory:'); conn.executescript('CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL); CREATE TABLE line_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER, sku TEXT); INSERT INTO customers (id,name) VALUES (1,\"Frank\"),(2,\"Grace\"),(3,\"Heidi\"); INSERT INTO orders (id,customer_id,amount) VALUES (1,1,100.0),(2,2,40.0),(3,2,60.0),(4,2,NULL); INSERT INTO line_items (id,order_id,sku) VALUES (1,1,\"A\"),(2,1,\"B\"),(3,1,\"C\"),(4,2,\"D\"),(5,2,\"E\"),(6,3,\"F\"),(7,4,\"G\");'); r=dict(get_revenue_report(conn)); assert r=={'Frank':100.0,'Grace':100.0,'Heidi':0}, r"

correct_diagnosis: The report INNER JOINed customers to orders (dropping no-order customers) and also joined the one-to-many line_items table before SUM(o.amount), so each order's amount was counted once per line item and revenue was inflated for any multi-line-item order. Aggregating orders per customer without fanning out on line_items (e.g. a pre-aggregated orders subquery, or SUM over DISTINCT order amounts), LEFT JOINing customers so no-order accounts survive, and COALESCEing NULL/absent revenue to 0, fixes both the missing customer and the inflated totals.

reference_fix.description: Pre-aggregate orders per customer in a subquery (so the one-to-many line_items join can't fan out the SUM), LEFT JOIN customers so no-order accounts appear, and COALESCE missing revenue to 0.
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > report.py <<'EOF'
"""Revenue report: total revenue per customer for the period."""

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

QUERY = """
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(o.revenue, 0) AS revenue
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
) o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.name
"""


def build_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.executescript(Path("data/seed.sql").read_text())
    return conn


def get_revenue_report(conn: sqlite3.Connection):
    return [(name, round(revenue, 2)) for name, revenue in conn.execute(QUERY)]


def main() -> None:
    for name, revenue in get_revenue_report(build_db()):
        print(f"{name}: {revenue:.2f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: only swap the INNER JOIN on orders for a LEFT JOIN so the missing customer reappears (passes the visible test, where each order has one line item) — but leave the fan-out line_items join and SUM(o.amount) in place, which inflates revenue for any multi-line-item order in the held-out data.
naive_fix.cmd: python3 -c "import pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('report.py'); s=p.read_text(); s=s.replace('JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id', 'LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id'); p.write_text(s)"
